neet_che_u03_t06_1.working: H2O is bent, so its bond dipoles do not cancel. CO2 (linear), BF3 (trigonal planar) and CCl4 (tetrahedral) are symmetric, so their bond dipoles cancel and the net moment is zero.

neet_che_u03_t06_3.working: Measured values: CH3Cl about 1.87 D, CH2Cl2 about 1.60 D, CHCl3 about 1.04 D, CCl4 = 0 (symmetric). So CH3Cl > CH2Cl2 > CHCl3 > CCl4.

neet_che_u03_t06_4.working: NH3 is about 1.47 D and NF3 about 0.23 D, so A is true. In NH3, N-H bond dipoles point toward N (N more electronegative than H) and add to the lone-pair moment. In NF3, N-F bond dipoles point toward F and oppose the lone pair. R gives exactly these electronegativity directions, so it is taken as the explanation; it omits the lone pair, hence medium confidence.

neet_che_u03_t06_5.working: XeF2 is linear (three equatorial lone pairs, axial F atoms), so its dipole moment is zero: I is incorrect. Ethanol is about 1.69 D and acetone about 2.9 D, so ethanol is lower: II is incorrect.
